title: South Africans value science while unequal access, trusted channels and resource costs constrain participation
source_unit: South African Public Relationship with Science (SAPRS) 2022 Survey Results
geography: South Africa; nationally representative adults aged 16 and older

observations.period: Late 2022 fieldwork; SAPRS national sample reported in 2024/2026 dissemination

denominator.unit: South African adults aged 16+ in the realised nationally representative sample

promise_science_skills_youth.unit: mean score out of 100 for the promise of S&T skills for young people

environmental_concern.unit: mean score out of 100 for environmental concern

trust_scientists.unit: mean score out of 100 for trust in the work of scientists

trust_university_science_information.unit: mean score out of 100 for trust in S&T information from universities

observations.method: SAPRS instrument in Round 19 of the South African Social Attitudes Survey; face-to-face household interviews, three-stage probability sample across 500 small-area layers, weighted to population distributions.
observations.uncertainty: Index means describe attitudes and are not measures of scientific literacy, institutional performance, or actual educational and labor-market opportunity.
observations.subgroup: South African adults aged 16 and older; the study also reports province, education, socioeconomic, geographic and demographic differences.
observations.counterinterpretation: Positive science attitudes may reflect general aspiration or social desirability; they do not guarantee trust in every institution, policy, technology or scientific claim.

observations.period: Late 2022 fieldwork; digital access and science-information exposure

cell_phone_access.unit: percent reporting access to a cell phone

internet_access.unit: percent reporting some form of internet access

high_s_and_t_information_exposure.unit: percent reporting high exposure to S&T information

high_active_s_and_t_information_access.unit: percent actively accessing high amounts of S&T information

observations.method: Weighted SAPRS household survey; digital access, exposure and active consumption are separate measures.
observations.uncertainty: Access to a device or internet does not establish reliable bandwidth, affordability, content relevance, science comprehension, or sustained participation.
observations.subgroup: South African adults aged 16 and older, with substantial variation by education, socioeconomic status, age, employment and urban/rural geography.
observations.counterinterpretation: High mobile penetration can support broad information distribution even when active science-information consumption remains low; access is a condition, not a completed engagement pathway.

observations.period: Late 2022 fieldwork; source-specific trust in S&T news

television_science_news_trust.unit: percent trusting S&T information from television

radio_science_news_trust.unit: percent trusting S&T information from radio

internet_website_science_news_trust.unit: percent trusting S&T information from internet websites

social_media_science_news_trust.unit: percent trusting S&T information from social media

chat_app_science_news_trust.unit: percent trusting S&T information from online chat apps

observations.method: Weighted SAPRS survey asking respondents to rate trust in S&T news by media source.
observations.uncertainty: Trust ratings are source-level perceptions and do not validate accuracy, actual media use, or how people resolve conflicting claims.
observations.subgroup: South African adults aged 16 and older.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower trust in social and chat media could reflect healthy skepticism, unfamiliarity, or lower source visibility rather than a stable preference for traditional media in every context.

observations.period: Late 2022 fieldwork; participation and unequal access to engagement

community_science_engagement_mean.unit: mean score out of 100 for community-based science engagement

attraction_event_attendance_mean.unit: mean score out of 100 for attraction-based science-event attendance

online_apps_engagement_mean.unit: mean score out of 100 for use of online science-related apps

low_community_engagement.unit: percent reporting low community-based science engagement; 34% reported none and 10% high engagement

access_inequality_range.value: Daily internet use ranged from 15% to 85% across subgroups; exposure and consumption also varied sharply by education, socioeconomic status, geography and age.

observations.method: Weighted SAPRS engagement indices and subgroup comparisons; the report separately identifies engagement types and resource requirements.
observations.uncertainty: Composite engagement scores are not equivalent to participation counts, civic influence, scientific careers, or policy co-production.
observations.subgroup: South African adults aged 16 and older, stratified by social and geographic characteristics.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low measured participation may reflect limited opportunity, survey recall, or the instrument’s definition of engagement rather than lack of interest or rejection of science.

related_sources.claim: HSRC overview of the SAPRS programme, national sample design and five-year monitoring purpose.
South African Department of Science, Technology and Innovation summary of the survey’s public-interest findings.

boundary: This record adds a science-legitimacy and participation mechanism: high perceived promise and moderate trust coexist with low active information consumption and resource-sensitive engagement. It is a 2022 nationally representative survey disseminated through later reports and 2026 public discussion; it does not establish current 2026 levels, causal effects, scientific literacy, or realized institutional inclusion.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The full SAPRS 2022 Survey Results PDF, HSRC programme page, and South African government summary were reviewed for sample design, science-value indices, digital access, source-specific trust, information exposure, engagement scores and subgroup boundaries.
